tiers.name: Fully human
tiers.short: No AI at any stage. Deterministic tools only.
tiers.means: No AI was used at any stage: not for ideas, drafting, editing or checking. Deterministic tools such as spellcheck, calculators, filters, compilers and search engines are fine.
examples: A hand-drawn illustration, scanned and colour-corrected.
An essay written and edited without any assistant.
Code written with a linter and non-AI autocomplete.
tiers.boundary: If an AI system proofread, reviewed or touched up the work, use HC.

tiers.name: Human, checked
tiers.short: Made by a person. AI only checked it or made minor fixes that don't change the content.
tiers.means: A person made all of it. AI was used only to check the work or for minor touch-ups that don't change the content: proofreading, fixing grammar and typos, simple rewording, flagging bugs.
examples: An article proofread by an AI, with grammar and typos fixed.
Code reviewed by an AI reviewer, with a few renames accepted.
A translation done by hand and sanity-checked with an AI.
tiers.boundary: If AI wrote new passages, added ideas or changed what the work says, use M1.

tiers.name: Mixed, human-leaning
tiers.short: Mostly human-made. AI contributed some content late in the process.
tiers.means: Mostly human-made. AI contributed real content, but late and lightly: rewriting passages, filling small gaps, generating a small part near the end of the process.
examples: A blog post drafted by hand, with a few paragraphs rewritten by AI.
A photo edited by hand, with one AI object removal.
A codebase written by hand, with some AI-suggested functions.
tiers.boundary: If AI shaped the work from early on, or produced around half of it, use M2.

tiers.name: Mixed, even split
tiers.short: Roughly half human, half AI, throughout.
tiers.means: Roughly half and half. Human and AI both produced substantial parts of the work, throughout the process.
examples: A report where AI drafted sections and the author rewrote and added the rest.
A song with human vocals and lyrics over AI-generated instrumentation.
This website: designed by a person, built with an AI.
tiers.boundary: If AI clearly produced most of the final work, use A1.

tiers.name: Mostly automated
tiers.short: Mostly AI output. A person prompted, steered, tested and verified.
tiers.means: AI produced most of the work. A person directed it closely: prompting, steering, testing and verifying along the way.
examples: An app built by a coding agent, with a developer reviewing and testing each step.
An article generated from an outline, then fact-checked and revised by the author.
A data analysis run by an assistant, with the analyst checking each result.
tiers.boundary: If the person only wrote prompts and gave the result one final check, use A2.

tiers.name: Almost fully automated
tiers.short: Almost entirely AI. A person prompted it and did a final check.
tiers.means: AI produced nearly everything. A person supplied the prompts and gave the result a final check before release, with little intervention in between.
examples: Images generated from a prompt and picked from a batch.
A summary generated by a model and skimmed before sending.
A script written by an agent and run once to confirm it works.
tiers.boundary: If nobody checked this specific output before release, use AF.

tiers.name: Fully automated
tiers.short: 100% AI-generated. No human reviewed it before release.
tiers.means: Generated and released with no human review. Nobody checked this specific output before you saw it.
examples: Summaries, captions or translations published straight from a model.
Replies from an unattended chatbot or agent.
Bulk-generated product descriptions.
tiers.boundary: If a person looked it over before release, use A2.
